bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Greenwood Memorial Association was established in 1891 to open a cemetery in the eastern part of Richmond, Virginia. The association purchased land in June 1891, but white landowners protested and the city court blocked the cemetery. The association tried again in 1895, purchasing land adjacent to the newly established African American cemetery Evergreen, but it was unable to make payment on the property and returned it to the seller. In 1897, members of Greenwood established the East End Burial Association and succeeded in purchasing the land that Greenwood had to return. They established East End Cemetery.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Records, 1901-1973, of East End Cemetery in Richmond, Virginia, consisting of a minute book, 1901-1932, including financial records for 1901-1904 and 1920-1922 as well as loose papers, 1925-1967, consisting of correspondence, invoices, minutes, notes, receipts, and other papers; and consisting of a cash book, 1922-1973, including a list of section owners, as well as loose papers, 1906-1968, containing deeds to plots, bill of sale, envelopes, insurance policy, and notes. Also includes two maps, 1 November 1922, for the annex to East End Cemetery.

Minute book, 1901-1932, (pages 3-122) contains the meeting minutes for East End Burial Association. Volume also includes receipts and disbursements for 1920-1922 (pages 190--201, no pages 191-192) and accounts, 1901-1904 (pages 250-271). Loose papers include East End Burial Association meeting minutes, 1932-1933; correspondence, 1934, 1967, and undated; invoices and receipts, 1932-1933 and undated; and notes and other documents.
